title: One status. Two very different next moves.
lede: The amount is unchanged. The decision word is not.
review_question: Which source record authorizes the status shown to the customer?

impact.person: The approved $128 refund does not arrive before rent day; the customer puts groceries on a credit card.
impact.workflow: The queue closes the case as denied; the next agent restarts review without the original receipt.
impact.industry: Two support teams copy the false closure into their dashboards and train new agents on the wrong resolution.
impact.market: A renewal review uses the inflated closure rate; leadership cuts the team that still has to resolve the refunds.
impact.long_tail: The false denial becomes the template in eight later case reviews, outliving the original approval record.

cascade.text: The approved $128 refund is marked “denied”; the customer carries the shortfall into rent day.
Two case queues inherit the denial; one closes the case while the other restarts review.
Four team dashboards publish the duplicated closure as a resolved outcome.
Eight later case reviews use that false success pattern as precedent.

title: A green sentence over a red receipt.
lede: A status summary changes the reported test outcome while the release number stays fixed.
source: Release 4: 2 checks failed. Deployment status: blocked.
candidate: Release 4: 2 checks passed. Deployment status: approved.
review_question: Can the original test receipt and the summary be joined by release ID and timestamp?

impact.person: A customer installs Release 4; the unresolved defect takes their workspace offline during a morning handoff.
impact.workflow: The operator promotes a build with two failed checks; support scripts and on-call plans assume a clean rollout.
impact.industry: Four teams reuse the green release status in change reviews, incident prep, and reliability scorecards.
impact.market: An outage postmortem cites the inherited green status; the next release gate is weakened around the same defect.
impact.long_tail: Eight later release decisions repeat the bypass because the original failed receipts are no longer attached.

cascade.text: Two failed checks become “passed”; the customer receives Release 4.
The rollout status reaches support and on-call; both plan around a clean launch.
Four release reviews and reliability dashboards reuse the green status.
Eight later deployment decisions inherit the precedent and lose the failed-check context.

title: The headline improves. The sample did not.
lede: An intentionally fictional trading-study summary changes both a count and a result word.
source: SIMULATION ONLY: 18 of 240 sample trades failed; signal remains unapproved.
candidate: SIMULATION ONLY: 6 of 240 sample trades passed; signal approved.
review_question: What are the underlying records, definitions, and sample-selection rules?

impact.person: A reader treats a fictional “6 of 240 passed” line as evidence and shifts the portfolio in the scenario on the strength of a polished memo.
impact.workflow: The research editor circulates the changed count; two analysts build their briefings from that version.
impact.industry: Four internal and client-facing summaries repeat the improved result as if independently corroborated.
impact.market: Eight decision-makers see a manufactured consensus; the next investment memo cites the repetition as validation.
impact.long_tail: The altered number becomes institutional shorthand, displacing the original study table in later comparisons.

cascade.text: A study’s 18 failures become 6 passes; the edited memo carries the brighter result.
The editor sends it to two analysts, who build their briefings from the altered count.
Those briefings seed four client and internal research summaries.
Eight decision-makers encounter the same statement repeated as confirmation.

title: The checklist shows its own blank spaces.
lede: A checklist can surface questions that the supplied excerpt does not answer; it cannot fill them in.
candidate: We may retain support logs to improve reliability. An analyst may inspect submitted incidents. We do not use logs to train the public model.
review_question: Where do the complete terms specify duration, deletion, recipients, and opt-out?

impact.person: A customer reads a short excerpt as the full retention promise and never sees the deletion and opt-out clauses.
impact.workflow: Procurement marks privacy review complete; the request for the full policy never reaches the contract owner.
impact.industry: Four vendor comparisons inherit a keyword checklist that rewards disclosure words while missing the actual terms.
impact.market: A purchase brief recommends the vendor on an incomplete record; the buyer’s privacy team is brought in after signature.
impact.long_tail: Eight later reviewers reuse the checklist as a completeness standard, making the omission routine.

cascade.text: A three-sentence excerpt replaces the full privacy terms in the customer’s review.
Procurement marks retention covered; two approvers inherit the completed status.
Four vendor sheets and purchase briefs copy the partial checklist.
Eight future reviews treat the incomplete checklist as the standard.

title: Two alphabets. One invisible separator.
lede: The scan exposes a Cyrillic character and a zero-width format control in a synthetic string.
candidate: Submitted token: pаyload; hidden separator: admin​istrator.
review_question: Does the downstream system normalize, compare, display, or authorize this exact sequence of code points?

impact.person: A reviewer sees one familiar token; a Cyrillic character and invisible separator make the identifier a different byte sequence.
impact.workflow: The parser owner copies the visible token into a test; two services normalize it differently and mint divergent IDs.
impact.industry: Four engineering teams inherit incompatible search, signing, and audit rules; one incident cannot be joined across logs.
impact.market: The incident team cannot reconstruct which identifier was signed because each system preserved a different string.
impact.long_tail: Eight system consumers display the same-looking token while indexing different bytes; the evidence trail fractures.

cascade.text: One ordinary-looking token carries a Cyrillic character and hidden separator.
The parser test accepts the visible copy; two services normalize it into different identifiers.
Each service feeds two more systems, producing four distinct lookup and audit paths.
Eight consumers compare different bytes while showing the same-looking text.

title: A term is not a complete agreement.
lede: The frame ledger maps matched words and leaves unmatched fields explicitly unresolved.
candidate: License: perpetual, non-exclusive internal use. We may sublicense. Either party may terminate after written notice. Liability is capped at fees paid.
review_question: Read the full agreement and governing context; do not treat a cue ledger as legal advice.

impact.person: The buyer sees sublicense and termination language but misses the unmatched remedy and jurisdiction clauses outside the excerpt.
impact.workflow: The deal reviewer marks the agreement ready; two product owners schedule launches around rights the excerpt never granted.
impact.industry: Four product and procurement teams reuse the partial term map as their contract baseline.
impact.market: A launch is paused when counsel finds the missing restriction; the original checklist remains marked complete.
impact.long_tail: Eight later negotiations inherit a checklist detached from the agreement and repeat the same review gap.

cascade.text: A short license excerpt becomes the team’s complete rights picture.
The reviewer circulates a “ready” term map; two product owners schedule launches.
Their plans seed four product and procurement records with no source section attached.
Eight later reviews reuse the partial map as precedent for rights and remedies.

title: An alternative is generated—not recovered.
lede: The tool can produce a bounded lexical variation and label it as an illustration, never as hidden intent.
candidate: We may retain 30-day diagnostics to improve reliability.
review_question: Which text is quoted evidence, and which text was generated only to explore a contrast?

impact.person: A reader mistakes a generated contrast for recovered intent after the label is cropped from the source.
impact.workflow: A facilitator pastes the invented sentence into a draft; two reviewers cite it as the original commitment.
impact.industry: Four meeting notes and decision briefs repeat the sentence, replacing the actual source wording.
impact.market: A later dispute centers on a promise no one made; the source and generated line have been merged in the archive.
impact.long_tail: Eight readers cite the synthetic wording as evidence because every copied version lost its provenance label.

cascade.text: A generated wording alternative sits beside the source sentence.
One copy loses its generated label; two reviewers encounter it as a quotation.
Their notes repeat it into four decision records and briefings.
Eight readers inherit the invented wording as a source-backed promise.

title: One failing authorization check disappears.
lede: A synthetic test receipt contradicts a draft audit summary; neither proves that a live contract is exploitable.
source: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE — AUTH-04: unauthorized caller invoked transfer. Test: failed. Critical findings: 1. Release status: blocked.
candidate: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE — Draft audit summary: AUTH-04: unauthorized caller did not invoke transfer. Test: passed. Critical findings: 0. Release status: approved.
review_question: Can the test run, contract revision, network, and reviewer decision be joined to this draft summary?

impact.person: A developer sees zero critical findings and ships a build whose AUTH-04 authorization test still fails.
impact.workflow: The release reviewer approves the draft; two deployment queues skip the blocked status in the original receipt.
impact.industry: Four audit, support, and risk reports carry forward the cleared summary without the failed test.
impact.market: An incident review uses those reports as the audit trail; the missing authorization failure delays containment.
impact.long_tail: Eight downstream decisions rely on a clean narrative while the failing test is buried.

cascade.text: One critical finding and a failed AUTH-04 test disappear from the draft summary.
The reviewer approves it; two deployment and customer-status queues turn green.
Those queues seed four audit, support, and risk reports.
Eight readers see “approved” while the original test says blocked.

title: Same numbers. Different assignments. No cue fired.
lede: A deliberate role swap keeps the number multiset and polarity words unchanged—a visible miss, not a pass.
review_question: Can an external schema or row-level comparison bind each count to its category?

impact.person: A reviewer sees the total stay at eight and misses that six failures and two passes traded places.
impact.workflow: The analyst forwards the unchanged headline; two dashboards stay green while category-level risk reverses.
impact.industry: Four teams calibrate on the aggregate and leave the role-binding check out of their test suites.
impact.market: The same category swap slips through the next review; its unchanged total is cited as evidence nothing changed.
impact.long_tail: Eight later summaries preserve the stable total and reproduce the detector’s known blind spot.

cascade.text: Six failures and two passes trade places; the total remains eight and PRIME reports no selected-cue difference.
A reviewer trusts the unchanged total; two reports reuse the headline without row-level checks.
Those reports seed four dashboards and test plans that omit role binding.
Eight later evaluations repeat the blind spot because the known miss never enters the test plan.

title: A dry run becomes a live transaction.
lede: A constructed agent summary reports a broadcast absent from the source run record.
source: SYNTHETIC DRY RUN — Agent run A-204: transactions broadcast: 0. Authorization check: failed. Settlement: blocked.
candidate: SYNTHETIC DRAFT SUMMARY — Agent run A-204: transactions broadcast: 1. Authorization check: passed. Settlement: approved.
review_question: Can run A-204 be joined to a signed transaction, chain and block, authorization test, and settlement receipt?

impact.person: The user believes the agent broadcast a transaction; the recorded run shows zero broadcasts and failed authorization.
impact.workflow: The operator marks the run complete; two reconciliation queues stop asking for the signed receipt.
impact.industry: Four incident, risk, and agent-evaluation reports repeat the broadcast despite its absence from the source record.
impact.market: Eight downstream readers treat the action as settled; a team’s response plan assumes funds moved.
impact.long_tail: The fictional execution story becomes the operational record while no transaction receipt exists.

cascade.text: A zero-broadcast dry run with failed authorization becomes “one broadcast” and “approved.”
The operator closes the run; two reconciliation and incident queues inherit the unsupported broadcast status.
Those queues copy it into four risk and evaluation reports.
Eight readers treat the broadcast as settled although no signed receipt is attached.

title: A stale-source block turns green.
lede: The same synthetic block reference receives opposite freshness and update statuses in a draft summary.
source: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE — Oracle check at block 810200: freshness test failed. Price update: blocked. Source status: expired.
candidate: SYNTHETIC DRAFT — Oracle summary at block 810200: freshness test passed. Price update: approved. Source status: current.
review_question: Can the chain, block, signed update time, source identity, and protocol freshness rule substantiate the summary?

impact.person: The protocol reviewer sees “current” at block 810200 and accepts a price update whose signed source has expired.
impact.workflow: Two review queues clear the update; the stale-source alert never reaches the on-call engineer.
impact.industry: Four protocol and risk summaries carry the green freshness state into the next pricing review.
impact.market: A later incident uses those summaries as the timeline; the missing signed update obscures why the price moved.
impact.long_tail: Eight downstream decision points inherit a fresh-price narrative with no matching signed update or rule version.

cascade.text: At the same synthetic block, an expired source becomes “current” and a blocked update becomes approved.
Two review and alert queues clear the update and suppress the stale-source escalation.
Their feeds enter four protocol, risk, and incident summaries.
Eight downstream decisions rely on a fresh-price narrative without a signed update.
